question: This control chart shows fill weights from six filling heads (H1-H6) of one rotary filler, one colour and marker shape per head (see the legend), all sampled at the same times. The centre line and the 1, 2 and 3 sigma lines are labelled on the right; they apply to every head. Sample numbers are labelled every 10th sample, with one light gridline per sample. Apply these rules to each head separately, and only these: Rule 1: one sample beyond 3 sigma (above UCL or below LCL). The signal is at that sample. Rule 2: two of any three consecutive samples beyond 2 sigma on the same side of the centre line. The signal is at the later of those two samples. Rule 3: four of any five consecutive samples beyond 1 sigma on the same side of the centre line. The signal is at the fourth of those samples. Rule 4: eight consecutive samples on the same side of the centre line. The signal is at the eighth sample. A sample exactly on a line is not beyond it. Which head is the first to signal, and at which sample number? Answer in the form: head number, sample number (for example: 4, 37).
scoring_note: sequence [head, sample]; our eval parses 'head, sample' (score.py int_pair)
references: NIST/SEMATECH e-Handbook, section 6.3, Shewhart control charts: https://www.itl.nist.gov/div898/handbook/pmc/section3/pmc3.htm
Western Electric Statistical Quality Control Handbook (1956), rules 1–4

question: Use the six document pages: the purchase order, two goods receipts, the main and split invoices, and the authorized amendment. question: Restore the masked photograph using the shuffled candidate patches. The photo panel is 1920 pixels wide and 2560 pixels high. Its origin (0,0) is the center of its upper-left pixel; x increases right to 1919, and y increases down to 2559. The page is displayed at reduced size: use its printed coordinate rulers, not page-image pixels. Ignore the surrounding page margins. The five gray regions are labeled H1-H5. For each hole, select the matching candidate letter and the transformation that restores the source photo. Estimate the hole center [x,y] in original-photo pixels; Euclidean error of at most 30 pixels is accepted. Apply undo_rotation_clockwise (0,90,180,270 degrees) FIRST, then undo_reflection ('none', 'horizontal' meaning a left-right flip, or 'vertical' meaning a top-bottom flip). Equivalent rotation/reflection combinations are accepted. Return only a JSON array of exactly five objects, each with hole_id (integer 1-5 matching the H label), center [x,y], candidate_id (printed letter), undo_rotation_clockwise, and undo_reflection. Array order does not matter. Use every hole once and each selected candidate once; the other candidates are distractors.
references: Warren LeMay, Urban Lab Building photograph, Wikimedia Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0
